author: reek
body: Four names the compiler used to promise and could not keep.

author: reek
body: list-files, list-directories, create-directory and write-binary-file were bound in the type environment and named in builtin-names, and no emitter for any of them was ever written. So a program using one resolved, type-checked, and then died at the very end of the build with CDX2040 -- an unresolved function offset. True, and no help at all to someone who had simply asked to list a directory.

author: reek
body: Three of the four are no longer phantoms. list-files and list-directories became real in Foreword chapter Fat16, and so did the write path: fat16-write-file and fat16-write-binary-file allocate a cluster, chain it, write the bytes and commit a directory entry. They are gone from builtin-names, so a chapter that wants them cites Fat16 and gets code that works, and a chapter that does not gets CDX3002 on the name -- which is the truth, and is what errors/fat16-write-needs-cite pins.

author: reek
body: create-directory was the fourth, and it is now gone the same way. It kept a binding in the type environment long after it left builtin-names, which is the worst of both: the name type-checked as a promise and then failed as CDX3002, Undefined name -- and that message was a lie, because the name WAS known. TypeEnv is the fourth table check-builtin-tables.ps1 cannot reach at all: it is a shadowing let-chain, not a list, so nothing caught the disagreement.

author: reek
body: The binding is removed, so CDX3002 is now the truth rather than a lie: the compiler does not offer create-directory as a builtin at all.

author: reek
body: The capability itself is delivered, and by the route this test predicted: fat16-create-directory in Foreword chapter Fat16 claims a cluster, zeroes it, writes the dot and dotdot entries and commits the parent's entry. So a chapter that wants to make a directory cites Fat16 and gets code that keeps its promise, and a chapter that does not gets CDX3002 on the bare name -- which is the truth, and is the same shape as list-files and the write path before it. What is gone is the promise in the type environment, not the ability; the four names this chapter is about have all ended the same way.

author: reek
body: A name the compiler promises and cannot keep is worth less than no name.
